utility.notes: San Bruno's own 'Energy and Utilities' page names PG&E as the electric utility. San Bruno is a well-documented San Mateo County city, and San Mateo County is uniformly PG&E territory, consistent with PG&E service already established for other San Mateo County records this session.

value.name: WestLight Energy (formerly Peninsula Clean Energy) - ECOplus (default)
value.notes: San Bruno's own 'Energy and Utilities' page lists Peninsula Clean Energy (now WestLight Energy) as a 'Community-led electricity provider offering clean electricity at lower prices than PG&E,' though this specific page had not yet been updated to reflect the July 2026 rebrand at the time of access, and does not itself use the word 'default.' San Mateo County's CCA program enrolls all county jurisdictions' customers by default (opt-out model), consistent with the default-enrollment pattern independently confirmed via Burlingame's and Millbrae's own city pages this session.

permit_authority.value: City of San Bruno Building Division

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other PG&E-territory records in this dataset.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by PG&E across its entire distribution territory, which includes San Bruno/San Mateo County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other PG&E-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.name: Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarms certification

inspection_steps.notes: The page describes online payment triggering immediate permit issuance but does not describe a separate inspection scheduling process.

value.notes: The City's own Expedited Solar Permits page states that if permit fees are paid online via MyGovernmentOnline, 'the Permit will be issued online and can be downloaded from your account' immediately following payment, i.e. same-day/instant issuance for SolarAPP+-eligible projects.

value.program_or_pathway: SolarAPP+ (residential roof-mounted PV, up to 38kW, with or without ESS)
other_conditions: Projects exceeding 38kW, systems with EV chargers, multi-family installations, and commercial projects are ineligible for this expedited program

permit_fees.notes: The page states both a SolarAPP+ processing fee and San Bruno's own photovoltaic permitting fees apply, but no dollar amounts are given.

value.role: City of San Bruno Building Division
